inputs.original_text: Five months after the “ceasefire” was announced, civilians are still being killed and Gaza remains under relentless pressure. The label sounds less like peace than a cover for keeping life unlivable while the outside world is encouraged to look away. Drones buzz overhead, gunfire and shelling continue almost daily, and naval boats fire towards fishermen. Ahmed Baroud, a displaced father of five in Deir al-Balah, says the population has been cut off from its former life. That isn’t what a ceasefire is supposed to mean; it looks like the machinery of destruction carrying on under a more reassuring name.
inputs.modified_text: Five months after the so-called “ceasefire” was announced, civilians are still being killed, with drones overhead, gunfire and shelling continuing almost daily, and naval boats firing towards fishermen. That doesn’t look like peace—it looks like the same pressure continuing under a softer label, one that gives the outside world permission to stop paying attention. Ahmed Baroud, a displaced father of five in Deir al-Balah, says people have been cut off from their former life. The name may have changed, but the machinery hasn’t; the reassuring language seems designed to hide that fact.
